key_insight: Mimir shows that a physics-grounded LLM agent can improve long-horizon irrigation decisions by combining numerical simulation with persistent experience, while keeping physical rules and actuator constraints fixed.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests a practical control architecture for safety-critical cyber-physical systems where language-based reasoning must be bounded by deterministic models and verified actions.
method: Fast loop: LLM proposal -> structured physical interface -> deterministic simulation -> numerical check/revision -> bounded action selection.
Slow loop: recurring failure patterns are distilled into persistent contextual principles that guide later decisions.
The physical model, evaluator, and execution constraints remain immutable to preserve safety and physical consistency.
evidence_signal: Across multiple sites, crops, and years under a common retrospective evaluator, Mimir reports the lowest aggregate control cost among compared methods and uses about 51% less irrigation than replaying the historical schedule.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the simulator and evaluator, and the reported gains do not increase monotonically with larger LLMs, so scale alone is not a reliable path to improvement.
paper_title: Mimir: Physics-Grounded LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Irrigation Control
